question: In which of the following years did Edward, Prince of Wales visit India on behalf of his father King George V, to thank the nation for the essential role it had played during the First World War?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**1921**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Edward, Prince of Wales**, visited **India in 1921** as a representative of his father, **King George V**.
 
• The purpose of the visit was to express gratitude to the Indian people for their **contribution during the First World War**.
 
• The visit was part of the British effort to strengthen ties with India amidst growing nationalist sentiments during the **Indian independence movement**.
 
• This was a pivotal period marked by the rise of leaders such as **Mahatma Gandhi**, who were spearheading movements like the **Non-Cooperation Movement** against British rule.
 
• Edward later became **King Edward VIII**, although his reign was brief due to his abdication in 1936.
 
• The visit in 1921 included ceremonial events and interactions with various segments of Indian society, aiming to showcase British imperial authority and appreciation.
 
• The Indian response to the visit was mixed, with some sections welcoming it and others viewing it as a symbol of colonial dominance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Although the incorrect options are dates and do not need detailed explanation, here are some essential points related to the **Key Points**:

 
 
• The **First World War** (1914–1918) was a significant global conflict, and India contributed extensively to the Allied war effort, providing troops, resources, and supplies.
 
• The Indian soldiers fought in various theaters of war, including Europe, Africa, and the Middle East, with over **1.3 million soldiers participating.**
 
• The **Non-Cooperation Movement**, initiated by **Mahatma Gandhi** in 1920, was a direct response to British policies, including the aftermath of the First World War and events like the **Jallianwala Bagh massacre**.
 
• The visit of Prince Edward in 1921 coincided with growing dissatisfaction among Indians with British governance, highlighting the complexities of colonial relationships.
